summary: Discovery with Saffron Labs about feasibility of moving inference from their vLLM/TGI-based stack to Redwood. Key concerns: eval parity, replication of current caching and hot-spot latency, SSO/KMS integrations for Private/VPC, and predictable cost for think-time workloads. Agreed next steps include a parity benchmark, security artifacts, and a technical deep dive for infra details.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (AE), Maya (SE), Evan (SE), Derek (Head of ML), Priya (Platform), Luis (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto): discuss migration lift, parity, hosting options, security docs

[00:00] Jordan: ok thanks everyone for joining, appreciate the time. quick intro — i'm jordan from redwood, i'm the AE on this account. maya and evan are with me for the infra bits. could we go round-robin quick intros?
[00:18] Derek: yeah hey i'm derek, head of ml at saffron. we run most inference on vLLM and a mix of TGI adapters right now, investigating options for reliability and cost predictability.
[00:28] Priya: priya here, platform eng, i own the k8s infra and our onprem gpu fleet. mainly interested in nets, VPCs, KMS and how you'd integrate.
[00:38] Luis: luis, cto. mostly here to listen.
[00:44] Maya: hi all, maya, se. we focus on model compatibility, latency SLOs and batching profiles.

[01:05] Jordan: high level, saffron — you're evaluating a few paths: keep onprem with vLLM/TGI, move to us hosted, or use our dedicated or private vpc. correct?
[01:15] Derek: that's right. the main trigger was we had a couple incidents where the autoscaler couldn't keep up and latency spiked for customer-facing flows. also cost went up with token rate when the seq lengths spiked.
[01:26] Evan: when you say seq length spiked, are we talking docs ingestion or chat-style sessions?
[01:31] Derek: mostly our knowledge assistant flows — typical 1.2k tokens but some edge cases hit 6k. average is 900-1.1k.

[01:52] Priya: we also need to ensure audit logs and KMS for keys, can't have cleartext exported. SOC2 is a checkbox for procurement.

[02:10] Jordan: noted. from a migration perspective we do a few things: 1) runway parity testing (latency & quality against your prompt set), 2) mapping model variants (open models + quantized variants), 3) deployment options and entitlements — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[02:40] Derek: question — our current stack uses vLLM with custom kernel hotpatches and a KV cache in front. how does redwood handle KV cache / prefix cache? will we lose that optimization?
[02:53] Maya: good question. we have prefix and kv caching built into the runtime; we expose cache semantics so you can maintain the same access patterns. it's automatic for repeated prefixes and we can pin a TTL. one caveat is cache hit behavior changes slightly across quantized kernels, we can show empirical numbers.
[03:14] Derek: ok ok, that sounds promising.

[03:30] Priya: network: for private deployment, do you require a managed control plane out-of-band? what's the egress pattern? we need to ensure traffic stays inside our VPC and keys never leave our KMS.
[03:42] Evan: for Redwood Private we offer a customer-managed VPC peering model. control plane metadata is optional, and keys can be integrated via your KMS/HSM — nothing unencrypted leaves the enclave. we do send metrics back if you opt in, but that's configurable.

[04:05] Derek: procurement will ask about SOC2/ISO, audit logs, retention. can you share the docs?
[04:12] Jordan: yes, i'll share SOC2 docs and a redacted audit log sample. i'll also send our network diagram and KMS integration notes.

[04:30] Luis: on the eval parity side, we need to ensure responses don't diverge. our prompt tuning relies on exact tokenization behavior from the current tokenizer and some custom TGI pre/post-processing. can redwood support that?
[04:45] Maya: we can accept custom tokenizers and provide a pre/post hook for deterministic transforms. we try to preserve tokenization parity but can also run A/Bs if there's drift.

[05:02] Derek: cost model — how do you price hosted vs dedicated? currently our op cost is driven by GPU hours + license for TGI.
[05:10] Jordan: hosted is per-token + compute bucket; dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with monthly commit. for your workload we can sketch a pilot price that models your average tokens and peak concurrency. we'll send a pricing sketch after we see the prompt suite and token distribution.

[05:36] Priya: autoscaling: we saw big spikes and the rollout policy was slow. how granular is your autoscaling and cold-start behavior?
[05:46] Maya: autoscaling is per-pool, sub-second scale-up for warm cache instances, and you can configure burst capacity to keep cold starts bounded. plus we support prioritized lanes for latency-critical traffic — that may help your customer flows.

[06:12] Derek: on the latency side we saw tail latencies go to 1.2s per token when the load hit a hot prefix; average was fine. can you reproduce that and show headroom?
[06:20] Evan: yes, that's part of the parity benchmark. we instrument per-token latency, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end p95/p99. Maya will run a run with your prompt set to mirror that.

[06:52] Jordan: competitors question — are you also talking to openai/anthropic or is this primarily self-hosted exploration?
[06:57] Derek: both — we have a pilot with openai for some features but the costs are ballooning and we lose hosting control. anthro is on the table but not primary.

[07:12] Priya: security: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML SSO and role-based controls so we can restrict who can push model artifacts and change deployment policies.
[07:22] Maya: supported — SAML/SSO+SCIM for user sync and fine-grained RBAC for model and route operations. audit trail is available per request.

[07:40] Derek: small nit — our prompt set depends on a zero-shot prefix, then multiple rerank passes. can your function-calling / structured output replace part of our TGI pre/post pipeline?
[07:52] Evan: we have function-calling semantics and structured outputs, and you can run reranker models as separate routes. many customers shift reranking to a dedicated route to better scale.

[08:10] Jordan: may i ask about timeline? when do you want to get a pilot going?
[08:14] Derek: we're aiming to have a pilot within Q4. procurement windows mean we'd like initial security docs and a price ballpark this month.

[08:30] Jordan: sounds reasonable. we'll prioritize the parity bench and security pack.

[09:00] Priya: ops question — if we go dedicated, can we bring our own nodes (BYO GPU) or is it Redwood-managed?
[09:10] Maya: Dedicated is typically redwood-managed for reliability and kernel optimization, but we do offer hybrid where you can federate local nodes into a pool with clear data residency controls — it's a more advanced architecture but possible.

[09:34] Derek: ok. curious about quantization: we use int4 quant on some models with custom kernels. are those kernels portable?
[09:41] Evan: we support quantized variants and have tuned kernels for int8/int4 on common archs. custom kernels can be integrated but require collaboration — we'll need samples to test parity.

[10:02] Jordan: let's talk about the benchmark plan (maya)?
[10:06] Maya: plan is: 1) ingest your prompt suite + tokenizer, 2) run a vLLM baseline in your config (you provide), 3) run same prompts on redwood hosted and dedicated quantized variants, capture: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), kv cache hit, and quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU or task-specific heuristics). we'll also capture cost at current token rates.

[10:40] Derek: for quality we care about semantic parity more than exact word-level metrics. can you run an embedding similarity or human eval for top 500 prompts?
[10:48] Maya: yes we can add embedding-based similarity and a small human eval for the most critical slices. we'll coordinate on the sample.

[11:05] Priya: how do rolling upgrades work for models? we need canary and rollback, especially for private.
[11:13] Evan: rollouts are supported: canary percentage, A/B by route, and automatic fallback to a pinned model version if regressions exceed thresholds. we also tie regressions to prompts/evals so you can block bad rollouts.

[11:36] Derek: wonder about tokens billing for our test harness — when we run a parity test, will that be charged on hosted?
[11:42] Jordan: for the pilot we can provide credit or include test runs in the pilot agreement; for production, hosted is per-token. dedicated is fixed resource with lower marginal cost.

[12:04] Priya: compliance — retention windows for logs: we need 7 years for some audit trails; do you support long-term retention?
[12:12] Maya: long-term retention is available as an add-on and you can export logs to your S3 or archive via our retention API.

[12:30] Derek: one last thing — we have a custom TGI preprocessor that rewrites prompts slightly to improve model behavior. can redwood run that as an inline transform?
[12:40] Evan: yes, we have a preprocessor hook and can run transforms either at the proxy or as a managed function. we'll capture latency overhead.

[13:02] Jordan: ok i'll recap before we close. agreed actions: derek provide prompt set + vLLM/TGI config, maya run parity bench, jordan send security docs and pricing sketch, and schedule infra deep dive next week.
[13:18] Derek: yep that's right. thanks everyone.

[13:30] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and a link to the benchmark runbook (will include columns for p95/p99/kv-hit/cost).

[13:45] End meeting.

Note: transcription had several imperfect tokens: TGI referred to as TG I in one place, vLLM sometimes transcribed as vLM. Names occasionally mis-spelled (Saffron as safforn).
